target_customer: People with hearing loss and general music listeners
problem: Music is hard to enjoy for people who cannot hear certain frequencies; the app shifts and balances audio to the listener's hearing test.
business_model: Free iOS app first, then hardware (Amp iPhone sound case sold on pre-order)

founders.name: Alex Selig
prior_employers: Microsoft (met co-founder during a gig there)
founders.background_notes: Grew up with hearing loss and wore hearing aids in both ears per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Varun Srinivasan
prior_employers: Microsoft (met co-founder during a gig there)

exit.reason: Company said it could not deliver the Amp case and had to wind down (May 2016 update).

competitors.name: BioAid
competitors.what: Free open-source iPhone hearing aid app from the University of Essex
competitors.traction_then: More than 20,000 downloads in over 90 countries by July 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: Audio signal processing personalized by a hearing test, then consumer hardware in an iPhone case; hardware was never delivered.

defensibility.rationale: Frequency shifting software is replicable; moat would have depended on the unshipped hardware.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; company wound down in 2016 before shipping.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2014-02) describes hard of hearing listeners unable to hear certain frequencies and the founder's own hearing loss; no spend data found.

branding.name_origin: Not found. YC page says the product line was marketed as Amp at ampaudio.com.
branding.domain_note: Hardware product ran on ampaudio.com per YC page; company legal name Symphonic Audio Technologies Corp per CB Insights summary.

identity.voice_and_tone: Founder story of hearing loss used in coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage focused on the product and funding; no evidence of community or merch.

pivots.why: TechCrunch (2014-02) said a hardware version working with any source was planned; Amp announced October 2014 per YC page.

outcome_analysis: SoundFocus raised a 1.7 million dollar seed in February 2014 and moved from a free app to the Amp hardware case. In May 2016 the founder said the company could not deliver the case and was winding down, and a DomainGang report mentions a Chapter 7 filing. The sources point to hardware delivery and funding failure but give no detailed post-mortem, so the factors are inferred from the stated inability to deliver.
notes: ampaudio.com returned 503. The May 2016 Medium post was seen only via search snippet (direct fetch blocked), shutdown details from that and DomainGang. Seed amount reported by TechCrunch and other outlets (VC Post, Hypebot, Xconomy per search); one aggregator says 2M. CB Insights total 1.72M. YC page lists August Capital Partners as investor but press does not; unverified. Chapter 7 case is from a reader comment, unverified.
